Promotional text vs description vs What's New

App Store Connect treats three copy slots differently on the zh-Hans localization row. This page covers promotional text only — the 170-character field that sits above the description on the product page:

  • Promotional text — up to 170 characters above the description. Often updatable without submitting a new binary (verify in Connect). The only above-the-fold China storefront slot many US/EU indie teams can change on a Tuesday for a feature launch, holiday theme, or time-limited offer.
  • Description — evergreen product copy below promotional text. Changing it typically ties to a version submission. Do not repeat your full feature list in the 170-character promo slot.
  • What's New — version-specific release notes submitted with each build. For update notes, see our What's New guide.

For title, subtitle, and keyword field work, see our Simplified Chinese keywords guide or China storefront listing guide.

  • Promotional text is easy to miss — it sits below screenshots and above the description, separate from title/subtitle fields in Connect
  • Teams localize title and description once at launch, then never revisit the zh-Hans promo row

Better zh-Hans promotional text gives returning China storefront visitors a reason to re-read your listing — it does not replace in-app UI localization or Apple review decisions.

The 170-character limit and no-review updates

Apple caps promotional text at 170 characters per locale. On the China Simplified Chinese storefront, that line appears above the description — the first text block many users read after skimming screenshots. Because promotional text can often be saved in App Store Connect without a new build, indie teams use it for timely news: a widget launch, a back-to-school theme, a privacy fix users asked for on social.

  • Count characters in zh-Hans before you paste — CJK glyphs and punctuation each consume the budget
  • Lead with what changed this week, not your entire value proposition
  • One or two crisp clauses: what launched, who benefits, any time limit
  • Match tone to your description — casual productivity app vs professional tool
  • Do not stuff search keywords — Apple indexes title, subtitle, keywords, and description for Search, not promotional text

What good zh-Hans promotional text looks like

Promotional text should read like a storefront headline, not a translated US tagline. zh-Hans and en-US promo lines can differ idiomatically when the news is the same:

  • Name the feature in plain Chinese: “新增桌面小组件，一键查看今日待办” not “优化用户体验，提升效率”
  • Call out a time-bound offer only when it is real: “限时免费解锁 Pro 主题”
  • Keep your English product voice — direct, specific, no unverifiable superlatives
  • Avoid mirroring comma-heavy brochure lines from your en-US page character-for-character
